title: Two Small Browser Games Built for Quick Play
author: Jason Lamb
excerpt: A look at the latest Coin Flip and Super Tic-Tac-Toe builds, with fresh desktop and mobile screenshots.

cover.alt: Super Tic-Tac-Toe nine-board game interface ready for a new match

content_html:
I have been polishing two small browser games with very different kinds of play. Coin Flip is a quick decision tool with a single interaction. Super Tic-Tac-Toe turns the familiar board into a linked nine-board strategy match.

Coin Flip

Coin Flip starts with an automatic toss and supports the coin, the button, and keyboard controls for later flips. Each result uses a browser cryptographic random bit, while reduced-motion preferences shorten the animation and suppress confetti. The shared-history panel shows totals and recent outcomes without exposing the private visitor metadata kept by the server.

Super Tic-Tac-Toe

Super Tic-Tac-Toe connects nine mini-boards. The cell selected in one board directs the next player to the matching board, and a completed destination opens the choice back up. The app also includes classic three-by-three, four-by-four, and five-by-five modes, computer difficulty levels, undo and redo, and optional private score history for signed-in members.
